hypotheses.justification: The conclusion only involves gradMatrix F x i j = spaceGrad (fun y => F y j) x i = fderiv ℝ (fun y => F y j) x (basisVec i). Write G y = F y j. From `he`, G (y + latticeShift k) = G y + (k j : ℝ) for every y. Mathlib has `fderiv_comp_add_right (a) : fderiv 𝕜 (fun x ↦ f (x + a)) x = fderiv 𝕜 f (x + a)` and `fderiv_add_const (c) : fderiv 𝕜 (fun y => f y + c) x = fderiv 𝕜 f x`. Neither needs differentiability. So fderiv ℝ G (x + latticeShift k) = fderiv ℝ (fun y => G (y + latticeShift k)) x = fderiv ℝ (fun y => G y + k j) x = fderiv ℝ G x. This holds in every case, including points where G is not differentiable, where both fderivs are the junk value 0. Rewrite the proof as: `intro k x; change fderiv ℝ (fun y => F y j) (x + latticeShift k) (basisVec i) = fderiv ℝ (fun y => F y j) x (basisVec i)`, then rewrite with `← fderiv_comp_add_right`, replace the function using `he` (the j-th component of `he k y`, via funext), and finish with `fderiv_add_const`. The hypothesis `he` is still needed. Nothing else in the statement mentions `hF`.
